explain.say: Whales breathe air through a blowhole, nostrils on top of their head, which seals shut when they dive. A Cuvier's beaked whale once stayed under for 222 minutes, almost four hours.

explain.say: Whales store most of their oxygen not in their lungs but in their blood and muscles. Their muscles are packed with myoglobin, a protein that holds oxygen and makes the meat almost black.

explain.say: Deep down, the water pressure squashes a whale's flexible ribcage and lungs flat. That pushes air out of the lungs, so less nitrogen gets into the blood, protecting the whale from the bends.

faq.a: A blowhole is a whale's nostril, moved to the top of the head so the whale can breathe while barely breaking the surface. Muscles seal it shut during a dive. Baleen whales have two, toothed whales one.
asks: Why is a whale's nose on top of its head?

faq.a: Mostly in their blood and muscles. Their muscles hold many times more myoglobin than ours, so much oxygen-carrying protein that whale muscle looks dark red to black.
asks: Why is whale meat so dark?

faq.q: Why don't whales get the bends?
faq.a: The bends happen when nitrogen from air in the lungs dissolves in blood under pressure, then forms bubbles on the way up. A whale's lungs collapse at depth, pushing air into stiff airways where little nitrogen gets into the blood.

faq.q: How slow does a whale's heart beat in a dive?
faq.a: Very slow. Scientists who stuck a sensor on a blue whale found its heart dropped to about two beats a minute at the deepest part of a dive, saving oxygen for the brain and heart.
asks: How slow is a blue whale's heartbeat?

faq.q: How long can a whale hold its breath?
faq.a: Many whales dive for 10 to 30 minutes. Sperm whales often stay under for about an hour, and the record is a Cuvier's beaked whale that stayed down for 222 minutes in 2020.

facts: A Cuvier's beaked whale was recorded staying underwater for 222 minutes, reported in 2020.
A tagged blue whale's heart rate fell to about 2 beats per minute during a deep feeding dive (Goldbogen and others, 2019).
